HIRAMOTO Tokutaro

educationalGoal: In this course, students will learn how to apply the concepts for innovation creation by SRI acquired in the Innovation Management course to various social situations. Specifically, the course will be incorporated into training for effective group discussions in job hunting activities.
advice:
In Japan, there is an urgent need to shift from rote learning to problem-finding and problem-solving education. In this context, there are increasing opportunities for elementary, junior high, and high school students to hone their ability to work in groups to find answers to unanswerable questions, including through exploratory activities. The number of students who enter universities through comprehensive selection and recommendations has been increasing in comparison to the number of students who enter through general examinations.
Under these circumstances, in order for students to make a good start in their desired careers, they must not only be able to do group work, but must also have the ability to produce higher results through group activities.
Based on this background, this course aims to help students learn how to apply the concepts for innovation creation by SRI, which they acquired in the Innovation Management course, in various social situations. Specifically, the course will be incorporated into training for effective group discussions in job hunting. In the class, students will actually conduct group discussions as exercises while receiving feedback from other groups and repeatedly making improvements, with the aim of acquiring advanced group discussion skills.
By utilizing videos and AI, students will also deepen their understanding of the evaluator's perspective , and based on this understanding, they will be able to envision their own ideal group discussion and deliverables.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              In Japan, there is an urgent need to shift from rote learning to problem-finding and problem-solving education. In this context, there are increasing opportunities for elementary, junior high, and high school students to hone their ability to work in groups to find answers to unanswerable questions, including through exploratory activities. The number of students who enter universities through comprehensive selection and recommendations has been increasing in comparison to the number of students who enter through general examinations.
Under these circumstances, in order for students to make a good start in their desired careers, they must not only be able to do group work, but must also have the ability to produce higher results through group activities.
Based on this background, this course aims to help students learn how to apply the concepts for innovation creation by SRI, which they acquired in the Innovation Management course, in various social situations. Specifically, the course will be incorporated into training for effective group discussions in job hunting. In the class, students will actually conduct group discussions as exercises while receiving feedback from other groups and repeatedly making improvements, with the aim of acquiring advanced group discussion skills.
By utilizing videos and AI, students will also deepen their understanding of the evaluator's perspective , and based on this understanding, they will be able to envision their own ideal group discussion and deliverables.
